purpose: Wall-clock build and test-compile costs, one record per measurement run, so later sessions can compare before/after a build-speed change. Append a new object to `runs`; never edit an old one. Narrative and caveats: docs/analysis/2026-09-29-build-time-baseline.md

rules: Use a REAL edit for incremental timings (append a fn to the file, build, restore). `touch` only changes the mtime; rustc's incremental cache then reuses everything and reports 3-4 s, which is not a real edit.
Nothing else CPU-heavy may run during a measurement (4 low-power cores): timings are wall clock.
Cold = no target/ directory. Warm = dependencies already built, only red_engine2 changes.
Record `cargo build --timings` HTML units (per-crate start and duration) for cold runs: the critical path is in there.
how_to_measure.edit_probe:
printf '
#[allow(dead_code)]
pub fn __probe_edit() -> u32 { 42 }
' >> src/sim/rules.rs   (restore the file afterwards)

changes_made: docs/HOSTING.md: Linux server build uses --profile fast
findings_about_the_project: RedEngineGames projects pin the engine two ways: reddm uses {path: ../../../RedEngine} (shares this checkout's target dir, no per-game rebuild); gravity-gauntlet uses {git, ref: d96b6c0...} (scripts/red clones it into .red/engine and builds it cold, about 5 min, and it is an OLDER engine than main).

A shared CARGO_TARGET_DIR across projects pinned to different engine commits is unsafe: the final binaries (target/<profile>/red_engine2) overwrite each other and scripts/red's staleness check (find src -newer binary) would treat the wrong binary as current. It needs copy-out to a per-project bin dir first.

Clients are built by RedEngineGames CI on a Windows runner from the cataloged RedEngine commit, so the shared Ubuntu server must be built from the same engine commit / wire protocol as the clients of the game it serves.
